name: 2013 Prairie Avenue — William H. Reid house (Beers, Clay & Dutton, 1894), K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B dwelling (D) lettered Fire Proof Construction'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: T-3625, piece 1 of T-1916 (the S07 package of the T-1837 programme), refines the T-2352 district draft in place under its id: the 1911 sheet's '3B' fireproof front block read at full size, and its street front built to the Inland Architect's February 1895 plate through a camera solved on it (data/reference_views/reid_house_2013_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json). The flanks and the rear, which only the 2003 nomination photographs show, are T-3626's; they stand here at the reconstructed tier (L-k01-2013-reid-3625).

documented_range.note: Standing in February 1895, when the Inland Architect publishes its plate of the house, and drawn on the 1911 sheet, which the T-1842 census rules present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). The record claims the 1904 target to the sheet's date and no more.

position.symbolic_location: 2013 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2013 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the '3B' front block on its north side, read off the 1911 sheet 35 raster at full size (px 1015, 476: where the block's south wall steps in to the narrower part behind it, on the line with 2011) through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, which carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this copy. The draft's corner stood 2.0 m further south and its body 5.5 m wide: the trace stopped where the sheet's lettering 'Fire Proof Construction' crosses the block. Rotation 179.383 degrees (the draft's) turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The '3B' front block, read at full size off the raster's own outline at 0.186 m a pixel: 18.2 m from the step in its south wall (px 1015) to the street front (px 917), 7.62 m from the north line (row 476) to the south line (row 517) — the 25 ft the 2003 nomination gives for a front that spans its whole lot. The narrower '3B' part behind it and the '2B' rear block stand on K01's rear wings.

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet over the front block, and three storeys over a raised basement in the 1895 plate.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the house yellow and letters it 'Fire Proof Construction' (the register's fireproof townhouse: a steel and concrete frame inside brick walls, which the 1911 label records as its construction class, not its face). The plate shows a stone basement under a pale brick front with stone and terra-cotta trim; the face is built as brick over a stone basement.

stone_front.note: The plate's basement: smooth stone in deep rusticated courses up to a projecting water table about the principal floor (about 1.65-1.75 m over grade through the camera, laid at the principal floor line, where K01 turns a stone basement to brick), the area lights cut in it. Its stone is RECONSTRUCTED as granite after the register's reading of the house ('granite basement'); the print is monochrome.

principal_floor_m.note: The portico's floor and the door's sill through the solved camera: the basement lights' heads at 1.33 m and the ground-floor sills at 2.45 m put the floor at about 1.6-1.65 m; built at 1.65 m, where the K07 and K01 stairs agree on nine risers.

storey_heights_m.note: Read off the plate through its solved camera, scaled on the 7.62 m front: the ground-floor caps' tops at 5.0 m, the second-storey sills on their band at 6.2 m and the third's at 9.7 m, the frieze's foot at about 13.0-13.2 m, the arched light's crown at 12.6 m under it. The top storey is built to 4.6 m so that K10's moulded cornice, whose section hangs about 0.57 m under the eave, stands where the plate's frieze and cornice do (about 13.0-14.2 m) clear of the arched light's head. The register's reading of the plans (10 ft ceilings on the main and second floors, a 12 ft ballroom on the third) fits the same storeys with a fireproof floor's depth between them.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A brick front on a fireproof frame: the contract's masonry starting thickness; no source measures it.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A 13 in brick party wall; no source measures it.

service_wall_brick.note: The side and rear walls, which the plate does not show, in the avenue's common brick (T-3626 reads them off the 2003 photographs).

face_brick.note: The plate's front is the palest on the block, paler than 2011's stone and 2017's brick, in fine courses; the register's 'cream textured brick'. The recipe's tone is RECONSTRUCTED: the print is monochrome.

street_front_trim.note: The plate: each ground-floor light under a moulded cap with a raised block at its middle (x 455-585 px, y 786-815), built as K09's corniced lintel; the upper lights stand in the pilastered frame without hoods.

wall_head.note: A heavy moulded stone cornice over a garlanded frieze across the whole front, the crown at about 14.2 m through the camera, its corona on a row of blocks (the plate's x 300-615 px, y 160-335). K10's moulded stone cornice stands for the frieze and cornice, its foot on the lunette's crown as the plate's frieze is; the frieze's garlands and wreaths are not carved (L-k01-2013-reid-3625). T-3626: the row of blocks under the corona is `blocks`, thirteen of K10's stone consoles 0.65 m apart (the plate's about 25 px apart along a front of about 300 px), 0.22 m tall, 0.18 m wide and 0.2 m out; the plate's are square modillions, the kit's console stands for them, its size and projection reconstructed (L-k10-2013-reid-blocks-3626).

roof_form.note: The plate shows no roof over the balustrade, and the 1911 sheet draws the block whole with no skylight or slope: a flat fireproof deck behind the parapet.

roof_pitch_deg.note: A flat deck's fall to the rear; not read.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's projection past the frieze, seen end-on at the north corner (x 300-335 px): about 0.6 m.

flat_balustrade.note: The plate's balustrade over the cornice runs the whole front between short pedestals at its ends, closely set turned balusters on a plinth under a broad rail (x 320-625 px, y 95-235), its top about 1.4 m over the crown.

window_kit.note: The plate's lights are one-over-one plate sash behind lace curtains; K06's two-over-two flat sash stands for them, the frame's broad middle light among them, and its round-headed fanlight sash for the arched light over the frame.

door_clear_height_m.note: The door behind the portico's columns, x 360-400 px, its head at about 3.9 m on the wall through the solved camera: about 2.2-2.3 m clear over the 1.65 m floor; built at 2.2 m, which leaves K01's lintel under the portico's soffit.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The portico's floor is the landing: about 1.6 m deep through the camera (its front columns' and its wall respond's x 335 and 412 px).

stoop_width_m.note: The stair under the portico, between its iron railings, about the portico's clear width between its columns.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the north end of the front, under the portico (K01's south: v runs south on this side of the avenue).

front_bays.note: Through the solved camera: the door centred about 1.3-1.5 m from the north corner; the ground floor's two lights at 4.0 and 5.8 m.

side_bays.note: No light in either party wall: the sheet draws 2011 and 2017 against them.

rear_bays.note: Two lights across the rear of the front block over the narrower part behind it; unseen (T-3626).

sash_by_storey.note: The ground floor's lights through the camera, sills 2.45 m and heads 4.58 m over grade, about 1.05 m across; the upper rows (the rear's) RECONSTRUCTED to the front's.

street_front_windows.note: Every light of the front as the plate draws it, through the solved camera (data/reference_views/reid_house_2013_prairie/inland_architect_plate.json): two tall lights under caps on the ground floor beside the portico; over them a frame of three lights a storey on the second and third floors, a broad light between two narrow ones at 2.36, 3.7 and 4.97 m, sills 6.2 and 9.7 m, heads 8.25 and 11.7 m; and the third floor's broad light carried up under a round arch to about 12.6 m. The band under the second-floor sills is the plate's projecting belt; the frieze of garlands and wreaths under the eave (x 330-605 px, y 245-335) is the wall head's (L-k01-2013-reid-3625). T-3626: the plate's stone frame round the three-light storeys is `frame`: a pilaster up each side of the frame and one in each pier between its lights, from the belt's top (5.95 m) to the hood (11.45 m); a sunk panel under each third-storey light between the floors (8.4-9.55 m, the plate's three rectangles under those lights); one corniced hood across the whole frame, 11.45-11.8 m. The plate draws the third storey's broad light as two: a square-headed light under the hood, its head at the hood, and a round-headed lunette over it in its own arch, so they are built so (1.2 m wide, 9.7-11.45 m; 0.9 m wide, 11.9-12.6 m), and the narrow lights' heads stand under the pilasters' capitals (1.6 m tall). The two oval lights at 0.83 and 6.54 m, 7.3 m up, each 0.75 by 1.2 m over its moulded ring (the plate's south ring x 565-602 px, y 590-670): no hole is cut, a dark field in a stone ring stands for the grilled light; the capitals are not carved (L-k01-2013-reid-3626). T-3626: the fifth frame strip (s 7.22-7.62 m) is the plate's border up the front's south edge (x 600-640 px), from under the frieze down past the second storey, carried to the belt's top (5.95-12.95 m), 0.4 m wide and 0.05 m proud; plain where the plate carves it, and its carved bracket at about 7.7 m not built (L-k10-2013-reid-blocks-3626).

basement_lights.note: Two square lights in the basement under the ground floor's two, x 455-585 px, y 1022-1085: heads 1.33 m, sills about 0.35 m, behind iron grilles.

chimneys.note: No stack shows over the balustrade in the plate; two stacks on the north party wall, set back where the plate cannot see them.

entrance_kit.note: The plate's portico over the door: two Ionic columns at its front and responds at the wall carrying an entablature at about 4.0-4.6 m (built 4.2-4.8 m, over the door's lintel), about 2.1 m wide and 1.6 m out (its columns at x 257 and 335 px, its wall respond at 412 px, through the solved camera), a stone balustrade on it as the second floor's balcony, and the stair rising to it. The front yard is the sheet's: the front stands 7.3 m behind the street line.

boundary.note: An iron fence on a stone curb just inside the street line (built 7.0 m out, clear of the public walk) with stone posts at the walk, as the plate shows it before 2011's and 2013's fronts.

yard.note: The yard's condition kit, as on the block's other refined houses.

rear_wings.note: The 1911 sheet behind the front block, read at full size: a narrower '3B' part 4.85 m deep (px 1015-1041) and 4.65 m wide along the north line (rows 476-501), with a small canted bay on its open south side, and the '2B' rear block 5.4 m deep (px 1041-1070) and 4.46 m wide. Their floors, storeys, flat roofs and lights are RECONSTRUCTED; the canted bay is not built (L-k01-2013-reid-3625, T-3626 reads the rear off the 2003 photographs).
